bullets.title: Quad 2 regime intact: Hedgeye bullish tech, short financials/small caps
bullets.body: Hedgeye's McCullough maintains Quad 2 positioning — strong dollar, higher bond yields, growth-over-value — with MSFT, NVDA, META comprising ~30% of index impact. S&P 500 upper Risk Range at 7,806; XLK printing new ATHs. Planning to reload shorts in IWM, XLF, Utilities, and XLI on relief rallies.

bullets.title: 10yr at 5.28%, but bond vol biased lower near-term — key test Oct 14-15 CPI/PPI
bullets.body: 22V and Morgan Stanley both flag that bond volatility (MOVE/VIX spread at 77th percentile) is more likely to compress toward VIX than vice versa. MS sees financial conditions only modestly restrictive (~0.78 SD) and expects two more 25bp hikes in Dec and Mar. Benign CPI/PPI on Oct 14-15 would drive meaningful repricing in rate-sensitive laggards.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler bond issuance contributing to long-end yield pressure
bullets.body: MSFT, META, AMZN, GOOGL, ORCL bond issuance equals 14% of net new Treasury supply over past 12 months, with 31% targeting 30yr+ maturities. 10yr yields rise ~5.4bps more in months following hyperscaler deals; continued capex expansion and weakening FCF-to-debt coverage suggest sustained upward pressure on long-end ahead.

bullets.title: Market breadth concerns: NDX near ATH but breadth at lowest since 2000
bullets.body: GS notes NDX up 13 of 15 sessions toward ATH with 10yr at 5.28%, while market breadth is the lowest since 2000 — tech/AI concentration driving gains at expense of broader participation. S&P 500 Q3 EPS growth expected at 27% YoY, highest heading into any earnings season since 2021. Bears cite AI trade resembling bubble with circular financing signs.

bullets.title: CEG surges 10% on 3.6 GW Google nuclear PPA — IPP/power sector re-engaged
bullets.body: Constellation Energy signed a 15-year 2.7 GW energy supply agreement plus a 20-year 890 MW new nuclear PPA with Google in PJM, enabling $4.3B+ in equipment investment across 11 nuclear units. Third major PJM deal in 2026 without 1-for-1 new generation requirement; positive read-through for TLN, VST, NRG. Sympathy moves: TLN +5.2%, VST +4.6%, OKLO +3.8% pre-market.

bullets.title: AI power crunch driving $240B behind-the-meter TAM through 2029
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley forecasts ~120 GW ($240bn) BTM power equipment TAM through 2029, as AI inference moves compute to the edge faster than grid can deliver. Bloom Energy SOFC ranks #1, BorgWarner Turbine Generator #2, FTAI aeroderivative #3. MS upgrades BWA to OW (PT $95 from $71) with distributed power business projecting $1.2bn EBITDA by 2030.

bullets.title: MRVL Investor Day: FY31 revenue guide $70-90B (55-60% CAGR), TAM expanded to $400B
bullets.body: Marvell raised FY28 revenue guidance to $20bn (vs. $18bn prior and $18.17bn consensus) and set FY31 target at $70-90bn vs. FactSet's $47bn consensus, representing 55-60% CAGR. Custom silicon revenue target $12bn in FY29 (3x FY28-29 growth); data center revenue +80% in FY28. Stock +8% intraday. CY30 TAM expanded from $100bn to $400bn.

bullets.title: Agentic AI to drive CPU TAM to $200B+ by 2030 — Mizuho upgrades AMD, SNDK, DELL
bullets.body: Mizuho raises AMD PT to $705 (from $580), SNDK to $2,050 (from $1,875), and DELL to $650 (from $600) on agentic AI expanding CPU TAM from $68B in 2026E to $209B by 2030E (32% CAGR). Agentic CPU alone reaches $80B (123% CAGR), growing from ~4% of CPU demand today to ~30% by 2030. NVDA GPU rack forecasts also raised: 72k NVL72 units in 2026, 85k in 2027.

bullets.title: Semis rally broad: SMH +6% w/w, AMD at 52-wk high +290% YTD, NVDA +4%
bullets.body: Semiconductor sector (SMH) rallied 6% week-over-week led by AMAT +11%, KLAC +9%, TSM +7%, NVDA +4%. AMD hit a 52-week high at $643 (+290.5% YTD); NVDA +29.2% YTD at $242.40; NET +70% YTD. Options skew at 5th percentile signals investors remain structurally bullish semis despite the run.

bullets.title: MU: CY27-28 supply significantly tighter than CY26; buyback pivot imminent
bullets.body: JPM notes Micron's CY27 and CY28 DRAM/NAND supply is significantly tighter than CY26, with demand growth well above low-20s DRAM and mid-20s NAND supply growth. HBM prices reset meaningfully higher in CY27 vs CY26. MU seeking materially larger buyback authorization and targeting 100% excess cash return. Nanya expects DRAM ASPs up ~10% QoQ in Q4 after 50% surge in Q3.

bullets.title: AI networking share shift: CSCO surging, NVDA's DC switch share slipping
bullets.body: JPM enterprise data shows NVDA's AI DC switch share declined to 44% in 2Q26 from 48% in 1Q26 while CSCO surged to 10% and is gaining rapidly; ANET fell to 20% from 22%. CRDO maintains 81% AEC dominance. AI, cybersecurity, and infrastructure are three distinct parallel 2027 budget pools per enterprise expert calls.

bullets.title: Agentic AI driving observability/monitoring spend — bullish DDOG, DT
bullets.body: Citi argues recursive agentic workloads create a telemetry multiplier effect (one prompt triggers many model calls and API hops), opening new SKUs for runtime/AI monitoring. DDOG positioned via Bits AI and AdaptiveML; DT benefits from Arize AI acquisition scale. Key risk: price deflation from higher data volumes and model providers embedding native monitoring functions.

bullets.title: German factory orders collapse -10.6% m/m; Eurozone slowdown risk rising
bullets.body: German real manufacturing orders plunged -10.6% m/m in August, with domestic capital goods orders down -28.6%. French industrial production came in at +0.3% YoY vs +1.2% consensus; French CAC down -10% from highs. Markets increasingly pricing ECB pivot toward bond-buying or rate cuts if contagion spreads; German PMI forecast to stall at 50.0 by July 2027.

bullets.title: TSM breaking ATHs ahead of earnings; GS raises 2027-28 capex forecasts to $85-98B
bullets.body: TSM is breaking all-time highs 10 days before earnings. Goldman raised 2027-2028 capex forecasts to $85bn/$98bn respectively and expects stable gross margins QoQ in 2H vs 2Q with out-year GMs improving as N2 ramp dilution moderates. Second Texas fab cluster expected to ramp 2030+.

bullets.title: Brazil upgraded to OW on Bolsonaro election momentum; BRL to 4.70-4.80
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgrades BRL to overweight and Brazil bonds following first-round election results showing Bolsonaro as favorite for Oct 25 runoff. Brazil equity trading at 8.8x 12M forward P/E; move to 10.9x implies ~23% upside. EM consensus also reduced Korea and Taiwan net underweights (to 2 and 27 from 7 and 30), and increased Mexico exposure.

bullets.title: Non-AI cyclicals (banks, transports, retail) lagged September — 22V sees better risk-reward
bullets.body: 22V upgrades MTB and KEY to Sector Outperform and WFC to Sector Perform, citing curve steepening (3M/5Y expanded from 55bps to 95bps), solid credit, and solid conference commentary from eleven banks. Bond vol compression would be the catalyst for catch-up trade in rate-sensitive names. Conference commentary universally positive on consumer and commercial backdrop.

bullets.title: AI cyberattack risk flagged as potential tail event for banks and semis/software
bullets.body: JPM flags AI-driven cyberattacks targeting South Korean banks (67k records leaked) and Daiwa Securities (110k clients at risk), with 12 AI-related cyber breaches tracked since mid-July across major platforms. An AI-driven attack on a US regional bank could trigger a flight to large-cap banks and a single-day dislocation in semis/software, though spending acceleration would follow.

bullets.title: AT&T forms fiber JV with GIP and CPP; targets 2.5x leverage within 3 years
bullets.body: AT&T forming a wholesale fiber JV (combining Forged Fiber 37 from Lumen and Gigapower) retaining 50%, with GIP and CPP each co-investing. Proceeds target net-debt-to-EBITDA of 2.5x within ~3 years and fund shareholder returns. Transaction expected to close H1 2027.

bullets.title: US August goods imports rise, signaling solid domestic demand; RevPAR tracking well above Q3 guidance
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's August trade data shows rising goods imports reflecting robust domestic demand. Separately, US hotel RevPAR is tracking +7.3% QTD vs Q3 guidance of +3.5-4.0%, with luxury RevPAR accelerating at +11.8% YoY; HLT and MAR likely to raise full-year guidance.

bullets.title: China Golden Week: stable traffic but per-capita spending contracting
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's early Golden Week read shows domestic mobility up only 0.3% YoY with ~1.5bn passenger trips. Shopping sales +5.3% YoY but traffic +3.4%, indicating spending compression. Hainan duty-free shopper count +13% but per-capita spending -7%; visible deceleration from Day 2. Outbound travel +6.5% diluting domestic consumption.
